q: A biological molecule is a chemical compound that naturally occurs in ______.
e: A biological molecule is a chemical compound that naturally occurs in living organisms. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. Non-living matter is not living organisms.

q: Carbon is an element present in all ______ biological molecules.
e: Carbon is an element present in all organic biological molecules. Organic biological molecules all contain carbon. Inorganic is different: inorganic substances may lack carbon chains; they are not the carbon-based macromolecules of cells.

q: Macromolecules made of long chains of monomers held together by chemical bonds are known as ______.
e: Macromolecules made of long chains of monomers held together by chemical bonds are known as polymers. Polymers are long chains of repeating monomers. Salts is not polymers.

q: Which of the following is NOT a polymer?
e: Lipids NOT a polymer? Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers. A polymer is a long chain of repeating monomers. Carbohydrates is different: carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: Water typically forms between ______ of the mass of most cells.
e: Water typically forms between 70% and 95% of the mass of most cells. Water typically makes up about 70 to 95 percent of a cell. 40% and 60% is not 70% and 95%.

q: In human cells, water is present at approximately ______.
e: In human cells, water is present at approximately 60%. 95% is not 60%.

q: Water molecules are polar because ______.
a: oxygen has a slight negative charge and hydrogen has a slight positive charge
hydrogen has a slight negative charge and oxygen has a slight positive charge
e: Water molecules are polar because oxygen has a slight negative charge and hydrogen has a slight positive charge. In water, oxygen is slightly negative and hydrogen slightly positive, not the reverse. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: The bond formed between water molecules due to their polarity is called a ______.
e: The bond formed between water molecules due to their polarity is called a hydrogen bond. Hydrogen bonds form because oxygen in water is slightly negative and hydrogen is slightly positive. Hydrogen bonds between water molecules give cohesion, solvent power, and thermal buffering. Covalent bond is not hydrogen bond.

q: Water has a high specific heat, which means it ______.
a: absorbs a lot of heat with little temperature change
e: Water has a high specific heat, which means it absorbs a lot of heat with little temperature change. Water absorbs a lot of heat with little temperature change, so it buffers cells. Dissolves only non-polar substances is not absorbs a lot of heat with little temperature change.

q: The property of water that allows sweat to cool the body is its ______.
e: The property of water that allows sweat to cool the body is its high heat of vaporization. Water's high heat of vaporization makes sweating and transpiration effective coolants. Low density as a solid is not high heat of vaporization.

q: Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves ______.
e: Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves all polar and ionic substances. Only gases is not all polar and ionic substances.

q: Cohesion in water refers to the tendency of water molecules to ______.
e: Cohesion in water refers to the tendency of water molecules to stick to each other. Cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other by hydrogen bonds. Stick to other surfaces is not stick to each other.

q: Adhesion of water contributes to ______ in plants.
e: Adhesion of water contributes to capillary action in plants. Respiration is different: respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: The density of water is highest at ______.
e: The density of water is highest at 4°C. 0°C is not 4°C.

q: Ice floats on liquid water because ______.
a: it is denser than liquid water
it is less dense than liquid water
e: Ice floats on liquid water because it is less dense than liquid water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. It contains air bubbles is not it is less dense than liquid water.

q: Carbohydrates are composed of ______.
e: Carbohydrates are composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Carbon and sulfur only is not carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

q: The general formula for monosaccharides is ______.
e: The general formula for monosaccharides is CnH2nOn. C2nHnOn is not CnH2nOn.

q: Triose sugars have ______ carbon atoms.
e: Triose sugars have 3 carbon atoms. 6 is not 3.

q: Pentose sugars include ______, which are components of nucleic acids.
e: Pentose sugars include ribose and deoxyribose, which are components of nucleic acids. Deoxyribose is the sugar in DNA. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information. Glucose and fructose is not ribose and deoxyribose.

q: Hexose sugars have the general formula ______.
e: Hexose sugars have the general formula C6H12O6. C3H6O3 is not C6H12O6.

q: Glucose exists in two ring isomers known as ______.
e: Glucose exists in two ring isomers known as α and β. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. D and L is not α and β.

q: Disaccharides are formed when two monosaccharides join via a ______.
e: Disaccharides are formed when two monosaccharides join via a glycosidic linkage. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Peptide bond is not glycosidic linkage.

q: Maltose is composed of ______.
e: Maltose is composed of glucose + glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Glucose + galactose is not glucose + glucose.

q: Sucrose is made up of ______.
e: Sucrose is made up of glucose and fructose. Fructose is an isomer of glucose found in many fruits. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Two fructose molecules is not glucose and fructose.

q: Lactose is a disaccharide found in ______.
e: Lactose is a disaccharide found in milk. Germinating seeds is not milk.

q: Polysaccharides are ______ in water.
e: Polysaccharides are insoluble in water. Volatile is not insoluble.

q: Cellulose is made of ______ subunits.
e: Cellulose is made of β-glucose subunits. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid. Fructose is different: fructose is an isomer of glucose found in many fruits.

q: Starch is composed of ______.
e: Starch is composed of amylose and amylopectin. Starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin. Ribose and deoxyribose is not amylose and amylopectin.

q: Amylose contains ______ glycosidic linkages.
e: Amylose contains α-1,4 only glycosidic linkages. A glycosidic bond joins sugar units in disaccharides and polysaccharides. Β-1,4 only is not α-1,4 only.

q: Amylopectin differs from amylose because it has ______.
e: Amylopectin differs from amylose because it has branches due to α-1,6 linkages. Β-glucose units is not branches due to α-1,6 linkages.

q: Glycogen is the main storage carbohydrate in ______.
e: Glycogen is the main storage carbohydrate in animals and fungi. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Plants is not animals and fungi.

q: Compared to amylopectin, glycogen has branches ______.
e: Compared to amylopectin, glycogen has branches more frequently (~every 10 units). Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Less frequently (~every 20 units) is not more frequently (~every 10 units).

q: Lipids are composed of ______.
e: Lipids are composed of glycerol and fatty acids. Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains that may be saturated or unsaturated. Glycerol combines with fatty acids to make a triglyceride. Nucleotides is different: nucleotides are the monomers of DNA and RNA.

q: Fatty acids in simple lipids usually contain ______ carbon atoms.
e: Fatty acids in simple lipids usually contain 12 to 22 carbon atoms. Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains that may be saturated or unsaturated. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers. 2 to 6 is not 12 to 22.

q: Plant lipids are often ______ fats.
e: Plant lipids are often unsaturated fats. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers. Trans is not unsaturated.

q: Animal lipids (except fish oil) are often ______ fats.
e: Animal lipids (except fish oil) are often saturated fats. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Unsaturated is not saturated.

q: Lipids store more energy per gram than ______.
e: Lipids store more energy per gram than both proteins and carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: A layer of fat under the skin provides ______.
e: A layer of fat under the skin provides heat insulation. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Structural support is not heat insulation.

q: Lipids help aquatic animals float because they are ______ than water.
e: Lipids help aquatic animals float because they are less dense than water. Lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers. Denser is not less dense.

q: Proteins are formed by joining many ______ with peptide bonds.
e: Proteins are formed by joining many amino acids with peptide bonds. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Fatty acids is different: fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains that may be saturated or unsaturated.

q: A peptide bond forms between the ______ of one amino acid and the ______ of another.
e: A peptide bond forms between the amine group; carboxyl group of one amino acid and the of another. A peptide bond joins the carboxyl of one amino acid to the amine of the next. Methyl group; amine group is not amine group; carboxyl group.

q: There are about ______ naturally occurring amino acids.
e: There are about 20 naturally occurring amino acids. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon. 30 is not 20.

q: The linear sequence of amino acids in a protein is its ______ structure.
e: The linear sequence of amino acids in a protein is its primary structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids. Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxyl group around a central carbon. Secondary is not primary.

q: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet are examples of ______ protein structure.
e: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet are examples of secondary protein structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Quaternary is not secondary.

q: Tertiary structure results primarily from interactions between ______.
e: Tertiary structure results primarily from interactions between R groups. Backbone atoms is not R groups.

q: Haemoglobin exhibits ______ protein structure.
e: Haemoglobin exhibits quaternary protein structure. Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen for transport. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Tertiary is not quaternary.

q: When a protein loses its shape due to heat or pH change, it is said to be ______.
e: When a protein loses its shape due to heat or pH change, it is said to be denatured. A denatured enzyme has lost its shape, so the active site no longer works. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Polymerized is not denatured.

q: Enzymes are mostly ______ that act as catalysts.
e: Enzymes are mostly proteins that act as catalysts. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Lipids is different: lipids include fats, oils, and membrane phospholipids; they are not true polymers.

q: Many enzyme names end in ______.
e: Many enzyme names end in -ase. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. -in is not -ase.

q: The specific region on an enzyme where the substrate binds is called the ______.
e: The specific region on an enzyme where the substrate binds is called the active site. The active site is the pocket where the substrate binds. The substrate is the molecule the enzyme acts on. Catalytic groove is not active site.

q: The 'lock and key model' describes the ______ between enzyme and substrate.
e: The 'lock and key model' describes the specific binding between enzyme and substrate. Enzymes are specific: each active site fits a limited set of substrates. The substrate is the molecule the enzyme acts on. Competitive inhibition is not specific binding.

q: A non-protein helper molecule required by some enzymes is called a ______.
e: A non-protein helper molecule required by some enzymes is called a cofactor. A cofactor is a non-protein helper, often a metal ion or coenzyme, that an enzyme needs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Substrate is different: the substrate is the molecule the enzyme acts on.

q: NAD is an example of a ______ derived from vitamin B complex.
e: NAD is an example of a coenzyme derived from vitamin B complex. A coenzyme is an organic cofactor, often made from a vitamin. Inhibitor is not coenzyme.

q: Deficiency of vitamin C causes ______.
e: Deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy. Scurvy is vitamin C deficiency, showing why nutrients matter in health. Beriberi is not scurvy.

q: Vitamin D helps bones absorb ______.
e: Vitamin D helps bones absorb calcium and phosphate. Sodium and potassium is not calcium and phosphate.

q: Nucleic acids contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and ______.
e: Nucleic acids contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorus. Nitrogen bases make nitrogen essential in DNA and RNA. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Sulfur is not phosphorus.

q: The two main types of nucleic acids are ______.
e: The two main types of nucleic acids are DNA and RNA. Nucleic acids DNA and RNA store and transfer genetic information. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. MRNA and tRNA is not DNA and RNA.

q: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a ______.
e: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base. Fatty acid is not phosphate group.

q: Adenine and guanine are classified as ______.
e: Adenine and guanine are classified as purines. Purines are the double-ring bases adenine and guanine. Sugars is not purines.

q: Cytosine and thymine are ______.
e: Cytosine and thymine are pyrimidines. Purines is different: purines are the double-ring bases adenine and guanine.

q: RNA contains ______ instead of thymine.
e: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine. Uracil replaces thymine in RNA. RNA is the nucleic acid that helps turn DNA information into protein. Guanine is not uracil.

q: DNA is ______ stranded, while RNA is ______ stranded.
e: DNA is double; single stranded, while RNA is stranded. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. RNA is the nucleic acid that helps turn DNA information into protein.

q: The pentose sugar in DNA is ______.
e: The pentose sugar in DNA is deoxyribose. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Ribose is different: ribose is the sugar in RNA.

q: The cell membrane is also called the ______.
e: The cell membrane is also called the plasma membrane. Membranes are phospholipid bilayers that control transport and keep compartments. Tonoplast is not plasma membrane.

q: The plasma membrane is primarily made of a bilayer of ______.
e: The plasma membrane is primarily made of a bilayer of phospholipids. The plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that controls what enters and leaves the cell. Carbohydrates is different: carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: In phospholipids, the phosphate head is ______.
e: In phospholipids, the phosphate head is hydrophilic. Hydrophilic heads face the watery surfaces of the membrane. Nonpolar is not hydrophilic.

q: The fatty acid tails of phospholipids are ______.
e: The fatty acid tails of phospholipids are hydrophobic. Hydrophobic tails hide from water in the membrane core. Hydrophilic is different: hydrophilic heads face the watery surfaces of the membrane.

q: Cholesterol in animal cell membranes helps to ______.
e: Cholesterol in animal cell membranes helps to maintain fluidity and stability. Cholesterol helps animal membranes stay fluid and stable. Increase permeability to ions is not maintain fluidity and stability.

q: Integral proteins may function as ______ in the membrane.
e: Integral proteins may function as channels or pumps in the membrane. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Waste products is not channels or pumps.

q: Carbohydrates on the cell surface are attached to proteins or lipids to form ______.
e: Carbohydrates on the cell surface are attached to proteins or lipids to form glycoproteins or glycolipids. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Nucleoproteins is not glycoproteins or glycolipids.

q: Carbohydrates on the cell membrane are important for ______.
e: Carbohydrates on the cell membrane are important for cell recognition. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Energy production is not cell recognition.

q: Passive transport does NOT require ______.
e: Passive transport does NOT require energy input. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised. A concentration gradient is not energy input.

q: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from ______.
e: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from high to low concentration. High to low concentration is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by ______.
e: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by simple diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Facilitated diffusion is different: facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient.

q: Facilitated diffusion uses ______ to transport substances.
e: Facilitated diffusion uses transport proteins to transport substances. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient. Endocytosis is not transport proteins.

q: Glucose enters red blood cells via ______.
e: Glucose enters red blood cells via facilitated diffusion. Facilitated diffusion uses membrane proteins but still follows the gradient. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range. Simple diffusion is not facilitated diffusion.

q: Osmosis is the net movement of ______ through a partially permeable membrane.
e: Osmosis is the net movement of water through a partially permeable membrane. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane. Ions is not water.

q: Water potential is higher in a ______ solution.
e: Water potential is higher in a dilute solution. Hypertonic is different: a hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells.

q: In a hypertonic solution, an animal cell will ______.
e: In a hypertonic solution, an animal cell will shrink (crenate). A hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells. Remain normal is not shrink (crenate).

q: In a hypotonic solution, a plant cell becomes ______.
e: In a hypotonic solution, a plant cell becomes turgid. A turgid cell is swollen with water and supports herbaceous shoots. A hypotonic solution has lower solute, so water enters the cell. Flaccid is not turgid.

q: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell is placed in a ______ solution.
e: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. A hypertonic solution has higher solute and draws water out of cells. Isotonic is different: an isotonic solution has the same water potential as the cell.

q: Active transport moves substances ______ the concentration gradient.
e: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. Down is different: an extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: Active transport requires ______.
e: Active transport requires carrier proteins and ATP. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. Channel proteins is not carrier proteins and ATP.

q: Cyanide stops active transport by inhibiting ______.
e: Cyanide stops active transport by inhibiting ATP production. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. Membrane fluidity is not ATP production.

q: Phagocytosis is also known as ______.
e: Phagocytosis is also known as cell eating. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Cell drinking is not cell eating.

q: Pinocytosis is the uptake of ______.
e: Pinocytosis is the uptake of liquids and dissolved solutes. Solid particles is not liquids and dissolved solutes.

q: Exocytosis is used for ______.
e: Exocytosis is used for waste egestion and secretion. Nutrient uptake is not waste egestion and secretion.

q: Endocytosis and exocytosis involve the formation of ______.
e: Endocytosis and exocytosis involve the formation of vesicles. Ribosomes is different: ribosomes assemble proteins; they are not the site of photosynthesis.
